test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: general
question: Sum Rs. 20000 and Rs. 40000 are given on simple interest at the rate of 10 percent and 15 percent per annum respectively for three years. What will be the total simple interest ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest (%) for P₁ = 10% × 3 = 30%

Effective interest (%) for P₂ = 15% × 3 = 45%

Total SI = (30% of 20000) + (45% of 40000)

Total SI = 6000 + 18000 = 24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹20000, Rate 1 (R₁) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹40000, Rate 2 (R₂) = 15% p.a., Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67a86a8f73ef461e6e944dd58b23281858ad02df1827e8422797c6373b7fe850.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (20000 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₁ = 200 × 10 × 3 = ₹6000

⇒ SI₂ = (40000 × 15 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 400 × 15 × 3 = ₹18000

⇒ Total SI = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ Total SI = 6000 + 18000

⇒ Total SI = ₹24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) in Simple Interest is given by A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Difference between SI and CI

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is P(R/100)².

Effective Rate of Interest

Effective annual rate for SI remains constant each year, whereas for CI it increases due to compounding.
